notes:
Docket 1.3.73

**Licensing: Docket will no longer buy an activation while it is already holding
one it cannot account for.**

An activation is recorded on your Mac alongside a hash of the key that bought it,
and it was only ever reused when that hash still matched. If anything changed the
hash — or left a receipt with no hash beside it — the seat was orphaned, and the
next run bought a replacement. The machine kept reporting "this Mac is not
activated yet" the whole time, because as far as the cache was concerned, it
wasn't.

That is the worst shape a licensing bug can take: your seats are finite, the
activations are real, and you cannot see them to release them.

Now, before buying anything, Docket checks whether a receipt it cannot attribute
is still live and adopts it if so, repairing the record so the next run does not
orphan it again. A receipt that is dead, or that belongs to a different key,
still activates exactly as before — a seat recorded against another key is left
strictly alone.

If your licence has fewer activations left than Macs you have set up, this is
likely why. `docket licence --release` frees the Mac you run it on.

**Also:** the "No HSTS header" fix now says that a host which cannot send
response headers cannot set it at all, instead of advising a change that host
does not allow.
